etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English agreable, from Old French agreable. Equivalent to agree +‎ -able.

definitions.definition: Able to agree; possible to be agreed.
Pleasant to the senses or the mind; pleasing, satisfying, palatable.

quote.citation: 1766, [Oliver Goldsmith], The Vicar of Wakefield: […], volume (please specify |volume=I or II), Salisbury, Wiltshire:  […]  B. Collins, for F[rancis] Newbery, […], →OCLC:

definitions.definition: (dated) Willing; ready to agree or consent.

quote.text: These Frenchmen give unto the said captain of Calais a great sum of money, so that he will be but content and agreeable that they may enter into the said town.

definitions.definition: Agreeing or suitable; followed by to, or rarely by with.

quote.citation: 1692, Roger L’Estrange, “ (please specify the fable number.) (please specify the name of the fable.)”, in Fables, of Æsop and Other Eminent Mythologists: […], London:  […]  R[ichard] Sare, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: That which is Agreeable to the Nature of one thing, is many times Contrary to the Nature of another.

quote.citation: 1883, Charles Colcock Jones, The History of Georgia: Revolutionary epoch:
quote.text: And I do not know of any Indian or Indians that have taken upon them to give up any lands to the White people other than agreeable to the treaty , nor would I accept of any but from the nation

definitions.definition: Something pleasing; anything that is agreeable.

quote.text: The disagreeables of travelling are necessary evils, to be encountered for the sake of the agreeables of resting and looking round you.
